en: Another important building block,
again, both when working with an agent or
when building an agent, is the model, the
brain.
In many cases, you wanna use very capable
cutting-edge models here because agentic
work is something that requires brainpower
and a smart model.
But it again also depends on what you're
building. If you're building a task-specific
agent with maybe only a few very specific
tools, You could build this agent as the
developer
with
less capable models, still not super small
bad models, but maybe not the cutting edge.
For general agents and general agentic tools
like Claude Cowork, on the other hand,
you typically want to use more capable
models or at least allow the user to select
that model. And that is indeed what many of
these agentic tools do.
In Claude Cowork, you can select which model
should tackle a certain task and you want to
use the more capable models for the more
complex tasks, and you can maybe use worse
models for
more trivial, simpler tasks. But that is, of
course, also something, again, to consider
as both the company building an agent and
the person using an agent.
